title: Codex-lift telemetry inverts the review pipeline's assumed hierarchy (codex_only 77 > claude_only 49, overlap only 14/140) — the single cross-model pass out-finds the multi-agent Claude review arm, the 'both-flag = high-confidence' synthesis rule almost never has material (1.4 findings/run), and the log tracks raw counts with no accepted/rejected disposition, so the designed ROI decision cannot actually be made from it

evidence.quote:
"total_claude_only": 49,
    "total_codex_only": 77,
    "total_both": 14
The `codex_only` count IS the cross-model lift — if it's consistently zero, the Codex pass isn't earning its quota cost and should be reconsidered.
Findings that BOTH critic and codex-adversary flag are high-confidence - the cross-model lift is exactly the findings only one side catches.

telemetry: 10 runs: claude_only 49, codex_only 77, both 14 (overlap = 10% of 140 distinct findings; both averages 1.4/run)
observe_how: The rule's own kill-criterion (codex_only consistently zero) is decisively NOT met — Codex earns its quota on this metric. But the inverse comparison is the real signal: a single gpt-5.5 pass produces 57% more unique findings than the parallel Opus critic+plan-reviewer arm. Three non-exclusive explanations the current schema cannot distinguish: Claude reviewers under-detect; finding granularity/dedup differs per source (one side splits, the other merges); or Codex over-reports unvalidated noise. Fix is one schema field: extend the codex-lift.jsonl row (emitted by /review and /premortem per codex-adversarial.md §Telemetry) with per-source accepted/rejected disposition recorded at synthesis time, then ROI = accepted-codex_only per quota-dollar becomes computable. Until then, treat 77-vs-49 as a precision-unknown count, not a verdict that the Claude review arm is redundant.
